You can have a good time brewing up widgets — as long as you don’t expect too much.
Aside from dealing with my calendar , there’s one thing I want AI to do: tell me if I’m about to miss the bus.
What I need is a widget. It needs to tell me real-time arrivals for the bus stop near my house. Tapping around on my phone screen to open the right app and select my stop will slow me down enough to miss a bus. I need glanceable information, and I hoped that Android’s vibe-coded widget feature could help me out here. It hasn’t, to my disappointment, but I still had a good time cooking up other widgets.
Google announced the ability to create custom widgets using AI back at I/O in the spring. It’s called Create My Widget, and it’s part of Android’s suite of “Gemini Intelligence” features. It’s in beta, and only just started rolling out to Pixel phones earlier this month. I was hyped. Not only does this feature raise tantalizing questions like “What is an app?” and “Where does the app live?” — stuff we live for here at The Verge dot com — it has potential to help me make my home screen ridiculous.
I fired it up on a Pixel 11 Pro and cooked up my first few widgets, including one that shows a different quote from Jurassic Park every hour — the original film, not any of the sequels, naturally. It took about 20 seconds to make, and it rules. Tapping the widget opens a thread in r/MovieQuotes, so there’s not much software magic going on under the hood, evidently. But did it bring me real joy to read the words “That is one big pile of shit,” on my home screen? It did.
I also made a widget that will display the words “Tut tut, looks like rain” whenever it’s raining. This is silly, and it accomplishes nothing except making me happy. I couldn’t think of anything clever it should say when there’s no rain, so it just says “No rain right now” otherwise. But I live in Seattle, so I’ll get a lot of mileage out of this widget.
The create-a-widget interface suggests a few ideas and categories, leaning on more practical uses like habit trackers and recipe inspiration. Fine, I’ll try something normal, I thought. I’m trying to get better about my daily mental health walk , so I had it make a widget for logging a week’s worth of walks. I was hoping for something visual that would trick my little monkey brain into keeping a streak going. Instead, I got something simply labeled “Log Walk” that triggers Gemini to add a walk to my calendar when I tap it. At least Gemini suggested the extra step of creating a checklist where I could mark off the days of the week as I completed my little walk.
It took me a minute to get my head around it, but many of the widgets are basically little prompt shortcuts for Gemini. You tap one, it pulls up the Gemini interface on your home screen, thinks for a while, then comes up with whatever you were asking for. The kinds of widgets you can make also seem to fit into some well-defined templates. You can create a widget that displays a countdown to a holiday or certain event on your calendar. You can show a recent score and upcoming game time for your favorite sports team. For anything more open ended, your widget will pull from Google search results (suggest a different three-ingredient cocktail recipe every day, for example) or prompt Gemini to figure it out for you. I was hoping for mini apps I could customize to my liking, but this is more of a one-size-fits-all feature. Fair, I guess.
I was hoping for mini apps I could customize to my liking, but this is more of a one-size-fits-all feature
That’s why my bus schedule widget didn’t really work out. I asked for a list of real-time arrivals; it gave me a tile that reads “Bus Arrivals” and uses Gemini to search for arrival times for the stop I specified. Gemini is helpful for some things but useless for this; it gives me a wordy response about how often the bus runs and when I might expect it to arrive based on the schedule. Not what I had in mind. On the bright side, my Jurassic Park quote widget had some words of wisdom for me: “Life, uh, finds a way.” That’ll do for now.

Keychron’s G6 HE uses magnetic switches like Logitech’s Superstrike mice, but the clicks are all off.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
When Keychron announced its $90 G6 HE gaming mouse, I immediately thought, “Cool! A cheaper alternative to the pricey $180 Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike .” Logitech’s innovation with the Superstrike is using magnetic Hall effect switches for a user-adjustable mouse click depth, with haptic vibrations mimicking the tactile click feel. The Keychron G6 HE , as its name indicates, also uses Hall effect switches for that same kind of customization. But something felt immediately off as I began testing it.
The mouse’s shape and design are very reminiscent of Logitech G Pro models, with more colorful flair. The magnetic switches are there and easily customizable (through a browser-based app, no less). But the clicks? The clicks are all wrong.
The left and right mouse buttons on the G6 HE use Keychron’s MagOptic switches , which are both magnetic Hall effect and optical. They click just like any standard mouse, regardless of where you set the actuation point. There are no fancy haptics on the Keychron. If you set the buttons to a shallow hair-trigger depth, you’ll register a press before you actually feel or hear any click. Set the depth for a very heavy press, and the mouse clicks before it actually registers. That… kind of defeats the purpose here.
There’s not much point in tuning the actuation depth of the G6 HE’s buttons if the click feel doesn’t match it. I suppose it’s still nice to have a hair-trigger-like setting for taking faster single shots in an FPS, but not feeling anything when you shoot is weird . And it gets frustrating when using the G6 HE as a regular mouse for productivity — like you’re getting phantom clicks as you mouse around your computer. At least I can feel my accidental clicks when using a Logitech Superstrike with the action set too high, and I know I’m to blame for leaving the mouse on my try-hard settings.
I reached out to Keychron for the reasoning behind the G6 HE’s magnetic-but-not-haptic setup, and cofounder Fab Chan said, “There are two reasons for this design. First, many users still prefer the feel of a traditional click over haptics. Second, a haptic motor adds weight, and for this model we prioritized a lighter design. That said, we’re planning a model with haptic feedback. It will be slightly heavier than the G6 HE, and we’ll share more details soon.”
The G6 HE is a lightweight mouse. It’s only 49g with its battery, or 40g in wired mode with the battery removed. The Logitech X2 Superstrike is 60g, and the newer X3 Superstrike is 59g — each still pretty light. If you ignore all the Hall effect stuff and just use the G6 HE as a regular mouse, it has some things going for it over the Superstrikes. In addition to its lighter build and much lower price, it feels a tiny bit comfier in my hand, thanks to its side walls that curve slightly inward at the bottom.
One of its best features is hot-swappable batteries. From my time testing Angry Miao’s AM Infinity Mouse , I know that once you can pop out a magnetic battery pack and quickly swap it, you never want to go back to plugging in your mouse to charge. You can also get the G6 HE in black with a standard built-in rechargeable battery for $15 less, but I don’t think that’s enough savings to forgo the convenience of hot-swap batteries.
The G6 HE’s charging base doubles as the wireless receiver, and of course it’s lit up with customizable RGB lighting. It has four programmable buttons for on-the-fly changes to things like DPI, lighting, mouse profiles, or just about anything else you want to program. The browser-based Keychron Launcher software is robust and makes tinkering with the G6 HE or its base very easy. And for some reason, the receiver / charging base is designed like a vacuum tube, which is fun, but it means you’re unscrewing its clear housing to access the battery — a little tedious.
I can’t shake my disappointment with the G6 HE’s lackadaisical magnetic switch implementation. Keychron seems proud of the fancy MagOptic Switch it put into the G6 HE, even going so far as to call it “next gen,” but this mouse seems a jack of all trades and master of none. The G6 HE is cheaper than most other mice with hot-swap batteries — which can still make it worthwhile if you don’t care about all the Hall effect stuff — but that is its lone saving grace.
We’ll have to wait and see if Keychron’s follow-up model with haptics can properly compete with the Superstrike mice and their hallmark feature. I’m excited to see where Hall effect tech goes in mice, and how more companies can evolve it, but the G6 HE is a half-measure.

Our favorite smart ring can track your sleep, activity, and more without requiring you to wear a smartwatch.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
If you’ve been curious about smart rings but have been put off by their high price tags, Black Friday is a good time to consider giving one a try. That’s because the Oura Ring 5 , which we consider the best smart ring you can buy, has dropped to an all-time low of $299 ($100 off) at Amazon , Best Buy , Walmart , and Oura’s online storefront for Black Friday.
Compared to the Ring 4 , the Oura Ring 5 offers a thinner, lighter, and more durable design that’s more comfortable to wear throughout the day and while sleeping. Like its predecessor, it can track your sleep, activity, heart rate, and other health metrics, giving you insights into your overall well-being without requiring you to constantly check a screen. It also offers roughly the same battery life and sensors as the prior model, though its new charging case supports wireless charging. (Unfortunately, the case is currently sold separately for $99 .)
Oura has also introduced several new software features, including Health Radar, which looks for potentially significant changes in your health. You can also import medical lab results, track GLP-1 medications, and access AI-assisted medical guidance through Oura’s partnership with Counsel Health. My colleague Victoria Song appreciated how the latter makes it easier to connect with an actual doctor, though she found it better suited for quick medical questions than more serious health concerns.
However, none of these software features are exclusive to the Ring 5, and you’ll still need a $5.99 monthly Oura membership to access most of its health insights. Given how similar the two generations are, we wouldn’t recommend upgrading if you already own a Ring 4. But if you’re new to smart rings, the current discount makes Oura’s latest model much more attractive, especially since it’s only $50 more than the Ring 4’s starting price.

Uraloğlu, Yenişehir Havalimanı YHT İstasyonu'nda gerçekleştirilen Osmaneli-Bursa Hattı ve Şehir Hastanesi Metrosu Test Sürüşü programında, Bursa'nın potansiyelini daha ileriye taşımak için ulaşım altyapısına önemli yatırımlar yaptıklarını söyledi.
Yapılacak test sürüşleriyle kentin hem yüksek hızlı tren ağına katılması hem de şehir içi raylı sistem ulaşımının güçlenmesi yolunda önemli bir aşamaya gelindiğini belirten Uraloğlu, "Günümüzde ulaşım, sadece insan ve yük taşımak değil, üretimi, kalkınmayı ve istihdamı birbirine bağlayan stratejik bir altyapıdır. Demir yolları ise bu altyapının en güçlü, en çevreci ve en ekonomik omurgasıdır." diye konuştu.
Demir yollarını 2002 yılından bu yana devlet politikası haline getirdiklerini aktaran Uraloğlu, şunları kaydetti:
"2002'de 10 bin 948 kilometre olan demir yolu ağımızı, 14 bin 272 kilometreye çıkardık. Sıfırdan inşa ettiğimiz hızlı tren ağımızı 2 bin 604 kilometreye ulaştırdık. Ankara, Eskişehir, Konya'dan İstanbul'a, Sivas'tan Karaman'a kadar birçok şehri, yüksek hızlı tren konforuyla buluşturduk. En son 9 Ekim'de hizmete açtığımız Çerkezköy-Kapıkule Hattı ile Tekirdağ, Kırklareli ve Edirne'yi de hızlı tren konforuna kavuşturduk. Böylece doğrudan yüksek hızlı trenle ulaşılabilen il sayısını, 11'den 14'e yükselttik. Çok yakında bu yolculuğa Bursa'yı da ekliyoruz. Osmaneli-Bursa Hattı'nın hizmete alınmasıyla hızlı trenle doğrudan ulaşılabilen il sayısını 15'e çıkarmış olacağız."
Uraloğlu, ticareti ve üretim gücüyle ülkenin lokomotif şehirlerinden Bursa'nın hızlı trenin sağladığı hız ve konforun yanı sıra yeni ulaşım ve ticaret imkanlarına da kavuşacağına dikkati çekerek, şöyle devam etti:
"Bandırma-Bursa-Yenişehir-Osmaneli Hızlı Tren Hattı, Ankara-İstanbul Yüksek Hızlı Tren Hattı'nın Bilecik varyantı sonrası Osmaneli'den sonra Bursa üzerinden Bandırma'ya bağlanacak. Hattımız, doğuda Osmaneli üzerinden Ankara-İstanbul Yüksek Hızlı Tren Hattı'na, batıda ise mevcut Kuşcenneti İstasyonu üzerinden Bandırma-İzmir demir yoluna bağlanacaktır. Proje kapsamında, Osmaneli, Yenişehir, Yenişehir Havalimanı, Gürsu, Bursa Gar, TEKNOSAB, Karacabey ve Dağkadı olmak üzere 8 istasyon inşa ediyoruz. Mevcut Kuşcenneti İstasyonu ile 9 istasyonla hizmet verecek bir hat oluşturuyoruz. Böylece Bursa'yı hem Ankara-İstanbul Yüksek Hızlı Tren Hattı'na hem de Bandırma üzerinden bölgesel demir yolu ve liman ağına bağlıyoruz."
Projenin mühendislik yönüne değinen Bakan Uraloğlu, şöyle konuştu:
"Osmaneli-Bursa arasındaki 106 kilometrelik kesimde, 21 ana tünel, 13 kaçış tüneli, 12 viyadük, 13 demir yolu köprüsü, 56 alt geçit, 25 üst geçit, 123 menfez ve çok sayıda diğer sanat yapılarıyla birlikte 369 sanat yapısını tamamladık. Bursa'yı hızlı tren ağımıza bağlayacak hattımızın en zor mühendislik imalatlarını tamamlayarak, hattın 106 kilometrelik Osmaneli-Bursa kesiminde altyapı ve üstyapı çalışmalarını tamamladık ve test süreçlerini başlattık. Bursa-Bandırma kesiminde yapım çalışmalarına devam ediyoruz."
Uraloğlu, testlerin ve sertifikasyon süreçlerinin tamamlanmasının ardından Bursa'da 2027 yılının ilk yarısı içinde hızlı tren seferlerine başlanacağını kaydetti.
Projenin Bursa'dan şehirler arası seyahat sürelerini önemli ölçüde kısaltacağını aktaran Uraloğlu, şu bilgileri verdi:
"Bursa'dan Ankara'ya ve İstanbul'a seyahat süresi yaklaşık 2 saat 15 dakikaya düşecek. Bursa-Bilecik 45 dakika, Bursa-Eskişehir 1 saat ve Bursa-Konya da 2 saat 50 dakika olacak. Proje, yolcu taşımacılığının yanında yük taşımacılığına da büyük hizmet sunacaktır. Hattın tamamının işletmeye alınmasıyla yıllık yaklaşık 30 milyon yolcu ve 60 milyon ton yük taşıma kapasitesine ulaşacağız. Bursa'nın sanayi ve üretim gücünü, raylar üzerinden limanlarımıza ve dünya pazarlarına bağlayacağız. Bursa-Bandırma kesiminin tamamlanmasıyla Bursa Teknoloji Organize Sanayi Bölgesi TEKNOSAB ve Karacabey, Kuşcenneti üzerinden Bandırma Limanı'na bağlanacak. Böylece otomotiv, makine ve kimya sanayisi başta olmak üzere bölgedeki üreticiler, yüksek hacimli yüklerini demir yoluyla limana ulaştırabilecek. Ayrıca Yenişehir Havalimanı İstasyonu ile havalimanına demir yolu bağlantısı sağlayarak hava ve demir yolu ulaşımını bütünleştireceğiz."
Bursa Gar'da Emek-YHT Gar-Şehir Hastanesi Metro Hattı, diğer adıyla Şehir Hastanesi Metrosu ile planlanan aktarma sayesinde kent merkezinden hızlı tren garına, gardan da Şehir Hastanesi'ne erişimin kolaylaşacağını vurgulayan Uraloğlu, böylece hızlı treni metroya, havalimanını demir yoluna, sanayi bölgelerini limanlara bağlayan bütüncül bir ulaşım ve lojistik ağı oluşturulacağını kaydetti.
Bu hatla mevcut Emek-Arabayatağı Metro Hattı'nın, Mudanya Bulvarı'nı geçerek önce Yüksek Hızlı Tren Garı'na, ardından Şehir Hastanesi'ne uzatıldığını ifade eden Uraloğlu, şunları kaydetti:
"Bursa'da halihazırda 40 kilometre metro ve 16,5 kilometre tramvay hattı olmak üzere toplam 56,5 kilometrelik bir kent içi raylı sistem ağı hizmet veriyor. Biz de bakanlık olarak üstlendiğimiz 6 kilometre uzunluğundaki Emek-Şehir Hastanesi Metro Hattı ile bu güçlü altyapıyı daha da ileriye taşıyoruz. Toplam 4 istasyondan oluşan hatla Bursa'nın şehir içi ulaşımına yeni bir nefes kazandırıyoruz. Hattımızın Emek-Balat arasındaki 1,1 kilometrelik ilk kesimini 2024'te vatandaşlarımızın kullanımına sunmuştuk. Şimdi de Geçit-Balat, Ahmet Yesevi, YHT Gar ve Şehir Hastanesi istasyonları arasındaki çalışmalarda önemli bir aşamaya geldik. Bu kesimde demir yolu işleri ve katener imalatlarını tamamladık. Hattı enerjilendirerek metro araçlarıyla test faaliyetlerini sürdürüyoruz. Projemizde genel fiziki ilerlemeyi yüzde 87 seviyesine ulaştırdık. Test ve hazırlık süreçlerini tamamlayarak bu hattı da 2027'nin ilk yarısında hizmete sunmayı hedefliyoruz."
Bakan Uraloğlu, mevcut metro hattını YHT Gar İstasyonu ile entegre ederek Bursa'yı hem kendi içinde hem de ülkenin diğer şehirleriyle raylar üzerinden birbirine bağlayacağını dile getirerek, "Böylece Kestel'den ve Üniversite'den Şehir Hastanesi'ne kadar kesintisiz raylı sistem ulaşımının önünü açıyoruz. YHT ile Bursa'ya gelenler, YHT Gar İstasyonu'ndan metroya aktarma yaparak şehrimizin önemli merkezlerine ve Şehir Hastanesi'ne kolaylıkla ulaşabilecek. Sağlık hizmetlerine erişimi kolaylaştıracak bu bağlantı, günlük hayata doğrudan dokunan çok önemli bir kazanım olacaktır." dedi.
Bursa'nın ulaşım geleceğini şekillendiren 2 projenin aynı büyük ulaşım vizyonunun birbirini tamamlayan parçaları olduğuna dikkati çeken Uraloğlu, Bursa'yı hem diğer şehirlere hem de kendi içindeki önemli merkezlere raylarla bağlayarak, kent ulaşımında yeni bir dönemin kapılarını araladıklarını da sözlerine ekledi.
Konuşmanın ardından Uraloğlu, trenin kokpitine bindi ve Bursa Valisi Erol Ayyıldız, TBMM Sanayi, Ticaret, Enerji, Tabii Kaynaklar, Bilgi ve Teknoloji Komisyonu Başkanı ve AK Parti Bursa Milletvekili Mustafa Varank, Büyükşehir Belediye Başkan Vekili Şahin Biba, AK Parti İl Başkanı Davut Gürkan ve beraberindekiler ile Yenişehir Havalimanı YHT İstasyonu'nu gezdi.
Daha sonra Yenişehir Havalimanı YHT İstasyonu'ndan test aracıyla Bursa YHT İstasyonu'na gelen Uraloğlu, bu istasyonda incelemelerde bulunduktan sonra Emek-YHT Gar-Şehir Hastanesi Metro Hattı'na geçip test sürüşü için bindiği metroyla Emek Metro İstasyonu'na geldi.

Yapay zeka teknolojilerinin şirketlerin çalışma biçimini değiştirmesi, iş gücü planlarını da etkiliyor. Şirketler yeni teknolojilere uyum sağlamak için farklı adımlar atarken Almanya merkezli yazılım şirketi SAP 'nin de kapsamlı bir yeniden yapılanmaya hazırlandığı bildiriliyor .
Bloomberg'in haberine göre SAP, bu süreçte en az 10 bin çalışanıyla yollarını ayırmayı değerlendiriyor. Konuya yakın kaynaklara dayandırılan habere göre işten çıkarmalar, SAP'nin dünya genelindeki çalışanlarının yüzde 9 'unu etkileyebilir. Ancak işten çıkarılacak kişilerin sayısı henüz kesinleşmiş değil. Bu sayının çalışanlarla yapılacak görüşmelerin ardından değişebileceği belirtiliyor.
SAP, Bloomberg'in gündeme getirdiği işten çıkarma planıyla ilgili açıklama yapmadı. Reuters da en az 10 bin kişinin işten çıkarılacağı yönündeki haberi kendi kaynaklarından doğrulayamadığını belirtti. Dolayısıyla SAP'nin böyle bir karar alıp almadığı henüz kesinleşmiş değil.
Öte yandan Kasım ayı teknoloji dünyasında işten çıkarma haberleriyle başladı. Önce Squarespace, çalışanlarının yaklaşık yüzde 19'unu işten çıkardı . Ardından Canva, çalışanlarının yüzde 22'sini kapsayan bir yeniden yapılanmaya gideceğini açıkladı . SAP'ye ilişkin son haber de teknoloji şirketlerinin değişen iş modelleri ve yapay zeka yatırımları doğrultusunda çalışan sayısını yeniden değerlendirdiği bir dönemde geldi.

Merino Wool May be a super fiber well worth owning , but it isn't cheap. Right now, one of my favorite merino wool companies, Unbound Merino , is having its once-a-year sale. Unbound Merino's Black Friday sale is a great chance to round out your travel wardrobe with some excellent merino wool. Better hurry though, unlike most sales this time of year, Unbound Merino's Black Friday sale ends tonight.
From casual, everyday T-shirts, to underwear, socks, and great merino travel pants, Unbound has a little something for everyone. We've combed through the site and found a few of our favorite deals. Be sure to see our guide to the Best Merino Wool T-shirts , Best Merino Wool Clothes , and the Best Base Layers for more great merino wool options.
Merino wool is great because you're stealing a sheep's ability to keep itself warm or cool based on the temperatures it's in. This is a process often referred to as thermoregulation. Merino sheep have thinner, softer wool than what most people think of when they think of wool. The sheep evolved this soft coat to keep them comfortable across a wide range of temperatures. The result is a fabric that's comfortable to wear next to your skin. For the softest tees, look for fabrics that are either superfine or ultrafine—anything 17 µm or higher—like Unbound's T-shirts.
Wool is sustainable, too. One sheep can produce 4 to 5 pounds of wool per year. While cotton has its place, and so does the occasional synthetic garment, merino wool is a remarkable fabric that's the cornerstone of my wardrobe. I don't think you can have too many merino pieces in your closet, but they’re not cheap, which is why we're featuring these deals.
I like Unbound's T-shirts because they're 100 percent merino wool, no synthetics involved. That means all the antibacterial, odor-resistant, moisture-wicking, temperature-regulating goodness of merino wool … just works. I've found Unbound's T-shirts in particular to be very quick-drying and wrinkle resistant, two of the reasons I think they're the best merino T-shirts for travel . The company's pants also have a very high wool percentage (95 percent), and they roll up nicely, making them very packable. Do you need special travel clothing? No, but Unbound's merino wool is naturally odor-resistant, which means you need fewer pieces in your bag . The company also offers a 30-day guarantee. If you don't like it, you can send it back.
Most merino products come with care instructions. Unbound Merino's T-shirts should be washed cold with like colors, then laid flat to dry. Whatever you do, don't bleach them and don't tumble dry them. The latter is especially destructive. I do it to every wool T-shirt I test, and it makes me sad, but I know some of you won't listen and will do it anyway, so I have to know what happens so I can warn you. Don't tumble dry . Just put it on a drying rack . It doesn't take more than a day. Seriously, you just spent $80 (on sale!) on a T-shirt; take care of it. Properly cared for, high-quality merino clothing like Unbound's is incredibly durable and will last for years. Throw it in the dryer and the pilling starts almost immediately.
Do I always lay them flat to dry? No. When traveling I usually hand-wash in the sink and then drape them over the shower curtain rod to dry, which hasn't seemed to have much negative impact. The issues with hanging wool to dry is that it will stretch out from the water weight. This is particularly true with 100 percent merino, like Unbound's T-shirts.
I've never had a problem storing merino in my closet between wears, but for long-term storage, I recommend you take precautions against moths, which are notorious for eating holes in wool. I have lost merino garments to moths. I make sure to wash and thoroughly dry whatever I am storing, then I seal it in a compression bag . Another option is to put your merino garment in a cotton bag or otherwise wrap it in cotton and then put it in a plastic bin. It's very important to make sure that the garment is completely dry before using any of these storage methods; otherwise your wool will smell musty and moldy. Other options include storing your garment in a cedar chest, which is a good natural deterrent for moths, or use moth traps or lavender sachets, which will repel the moths.
Unbound's T-shirts were my introduction to the brand, and they're still one of my favorite merino T-shirts . This T-shirt is incredibly soft, and because it's 100 percent merino wool, it'll stay odor-free for ages—as long as five or six days in my testing (depending on local temps, what you're doing, etc). Unbound's crew neck merino T-shirt has a relaxed, casual cut. It's not going for the technical look you'll get from many outdoor brands. It's also lightweight and packs down to a tiny ball, which is perfect if you're looking to simplify down to one bag . (Really, is there any other way to travel?)
The final thing I love about these is how fast they dry. In most climates, you can give it a wash in the sink at night, roll it up in a towel, wring it dry, lay it out flat, and it'll be dry by morning. If they have a downside, it's that Unbound's T-shirts do need to be babied a little. To help them last a long time I recommend hand washing and line-drying. Also note that while I like the merino crew neck, the V-neck is also on sale for $88 ($10 off) .
Unbound's merino travel pants are a light and comfortable merino blend, with plenty of stretch and freedom of moment, thanks to the 5 percent elastane. These have a more formal look, what you might call slacks if you are a certain type of person. You might even be able to pull off going to office in them, but I'd sooner chew my leg off than work in an office, so I don't really know. I can say I've worn them to nice restaurants without a second look, and yet they don't scream “I've got money” when you're stumbling back to your hotel room in Prague at 4 am.
As you would expect from anything Unbound makes, these pack down fantastically small. You can pack two pairs of these for every pair of jeans. Again, for serious travelers looking to live out of a single carry-on bag, that's huge. The only downside is that these are on the thin side, not something you'd want to wear alone in cold climates. If you're like me and have to deal with winter, throw a good base layer underneath them and you'll be fine. The slim fit pant is also on sale if that's more your style.
One of the best ways to save at the Unbound Merino Black Friday sale is to go for a bundle. I like this 1-Pack bundle, which gets you a T-shirt, underwear and socks for $125. There are quite a few other bundles as well, including the T-shirt 3-pack for $240 ($54 off) which is $20 cheaper than buying three T-shirts on sale, the boxer briefs pack for $75 ($15 off) , and the sock 3-pack which is a steal at just $40 ($38 off) .
Unbound's merino boxers are warm without being hot, great at wicking moisture, and capable of several wears without undue odors. 84 percent merino wool, 12 percent nylon, and 4 percent spandex, for a soft, stretchy, comfortable fit. They're 180 GSM (see our merino guide for exactly what GSM means), which makes them nice and light. The inseam here is 5.5 inches, and there's no tag, which is nice. The women's underwear is also on sale.
I prefer the short-sleeve T-shirts, but if you want a long sleeve, this is the T-shirt for you. It's essentially Unbound's short sleeve T-shirt, just long sleeve. All the same descriptions apply here, and many of the same multipack bundles are available. You can grab a 2-pack of long sleeve merino tees for $190 ($40 off) .

Yapay zeka ajanlarının web üzerinde kullanıcı adına işlem gerçekleştirmesi, son dönemde hem büyük teknoloji şirketlerinin hem de girişimlerin odaklandığı alanlardan biri haline geldi. Bu yıl Emre Sokullu tarafından geliştirilmeye başlanan WebBrain de bu alana açık kaynaklı ve model bağımsız bir yaklaşımla dahil oluyor. Sokullu, WebBrain'i kendi ihtiyacından yola çıkarak geliştirmeye başladığını belirtiyor. Amaç; tarayıcı içinde çalışan, kullanıcıların istedikleri yapay zeka modelini seçebildiği ve kaynak koduna erişebildiği bir asistan geliştirmek.
Chrome, Firefox ve Edge üzerinde çalışabilen WebBrain, kullanıcının açık olan web sayfalarını ve PDF dosyalarını okuyabilen içerik hakkında soruları yanıtlıyor. Ürün, veri toplama, sayfalardaki öğelerle etkileşim kurma ve çok adımlı görevleri yerine getirme gibi özellikler sunuyor. WebBrain'in mevcut özellikleri arasında sayfalardaki verileri yapılandırılmış şekilde çıkarma, form alanlarını doldurma, tıklama ve sayfalar arasında gezinme gibi işlemler de bulunuyor.
WebBrain'in arkasındaki isim olan Sokullu, daha önce sosyal ağ platformu Grou.ps 'u kurmuştu. Sokullu'nun aktardığına göre Grou.ps, döneminde aylık 8 milyon aktif kullanıcıy a ulaşmıştı. WebBrain projesi şu anda Sokullu tarafından yürütülürken geliştirme sürecine açık kaynak topluluğu da katkı sağlıyor. Tek bir yapay zeka modeline bağlı değil WebBrain'i benzer yapay zeka tarayıcı araçlarından ayıran temel noktalardan biri, ürünün tek bir yapay zeka modeline ya da sağlayıcısına bağlı olmaması.
Kullanıcılar Qwen, DeepSeek ve Gemma gibi açık modellerin yanı sıra OpenAI ve Anthropic gibi şirketlerin sunduğu modelleri tercih edebiliyor. Yerel modelleri çalıştırmak isteyen kullanıcılar ise llama.cpp, Ollama ve LM Studio gibi araçlardan yararlanabiliyor. WebBrain, OpenAI uyumlu API'lerin yanı sıra yerel modellerle çalışmanın desteklendiğini de belirtiliyor. Bu yaklaşım sayesinde kullanıcıların web sayfalarındaki verilerini mutlaka bir bulut servisine göndermesi gerekmiyor. Yerel model tercih edildiğinde yapay zeka işlemleri kullanıcının kendi cihazında gerçekleştirilebiliyor.
WebBrain ekibi aynı zamanda tarayıcı görevlerine özel daha küçük yapay zeka modelleri üzerinde çalışıyor. Bunlardan biri, Liquid AI'ın LFM3 mimarisi temel alınarak geliştirilen WebBrain Compass VLD v6 2B . 2 milyar parametreli model, özellikle tarayıcı ekranlarını anlama ve ajan tarafından gerçekleştirilecek işlemi belirleme görevleri için özelleştirilmiş durumda.
WebBrain'in paylaştığı testlerde model, 100 örnekten oluşan tarayıcı görsel anlama testinde 66 tam başarı elde ederken ortalama yüzde 90,2 değerlendirme puanına ulaştı. Testlerin tüketici sınıfı bir Nvidia RTX 5060 Ti üzerinde gerçekleştirildiğini de ekleyelim. Şirket, her işlem için mümkün olan en büyük yapay zeka modelini kullanmak yerine belirli görevlerde daha küçük ve cihaz üzerinde çalışabilecek modellerden yararlanmaya odaklanıyor.
Şirketin paylaştığı verilere göre WebBrain'in Chrome ve Firefox sürümleri toplamda 2 binin üzerinde aktif kullanıcıya sahip. Projenin GitHub deposu da yaklaşık 1.800 yıldız seviyesine ulaşmış durumda. WebBrain'in kullanıcı tabanı ağırlıklı olarak uluslararası pazarlardan oluşuyor. ABD, yaklaşık yüzde 20'lik payla ilk sırada yer alırken Hindistan yüzde 11 ile ikinci sırada bulunuyor. İngiltere, Kanada ve Fransa da WebBrain'in öne çıkan pazarları arasında. Emre Sokullu'nun aktardığına göre ürünün aktif kullanıcı sayısı bugüne kadar organik olarak yaklaşık üç ayda bir ikiye katlandı.
WebBrain'in bir diğer önemli parçası ise Chromium altyapısıyla geliştirilen Murshid tarayıcısı. WebBrain'i doğrudan bünyesinde barındıran Murshid, yapay zeka ajanının tarayıcı eklentilerinin getirdiği sınırlamaların ötesine geçmesini sağlıyor. Murshid, sekmeler arasında gezinme, dosya indirme ve adres çubuğundan arama yapma gibi standart tarayıcı özelliklerini sunarken WebBrain yapay zeka asistanını da ayrı bir eklenti yüklemeye gerek kalmadan kullanıma hazır hale getiriyor. Böylece kullanıcılar, yapay zeka asistanına tarayıcının yan panelinden erişebiliyor ve açık olan web sayfasıyla ilgili işlemleri doğrudan gerçekleştirebiliyor.
Sokullu, Murshid'i kullanıcıların Chrome veya mevcut tarayıcılarını tamamen bırakmasını gerektiren bir ürün olarak konumlandırmıyor. Bunun yerine yapay zeka ile gerçekleştirilen araştırma, veri toplama ve otomasyon işleri için ayrı bir çalışma ortamı sunmayı hedefliyor.
Bu alanda Perplexity Comet, Dia ve Claude'un tarayıcı araçları WebBrain'in aynı kullanıcı ihtiyacına farklı yöntemlerle yaklaşan rakipleri arasında gösteriliyor. WebBrain ise açık kaynaklı yapısı ve model seçme özgürlüğü ile rakiplerinden ayrışıyor. Kullanıcı ister kendi API anahtarını kullanabiliyor, ister yerel model çalıştırabiliyor, ister mevcut tarayıcısında WebBrain'i kullanarak çalışma düzenini değiştirmeden devam edebiliyor.
WebBrain'in açık kaynaklı yazılımı ücretsiz olarak sunuluyor. Kullanıcılar kendi yapay zeka API anahtarlarını veya yerel modellerini kullanmaları durumunda WebBrain'e ayrıca ücret ödemiyor. Model kurmak veya API sağlayıcılarıyla ayrı ayrı uğraşmak istemeyen kullanıcılar için ise Compass isimli ücretli yapay zeka hizmeti sunuluyor.
WebBrain'in gelir modeli Compass'ın kullanım paketleri ve abonelikleri üzerinden şekilleniyor. Dolayısıyla şirket, tarayıcı ajanının kullanıcı adına gerçekleştirdiği işlemler üzerinden komisyon alan bir pazaryeri modeli yerine yapay zeka altyapısına erişimi ücretlendiren bir abonelik modeli benimsiyor.
Şimdiye kadar dış yatırım almayan WeBrain Emre Sokullu'nun kendi kaynaklarıyla geliştirildi. Girişim, bir sonraki büyüme aşaması için yatırımcılar ve stratejik ortaklarla görüşmeler yürütüyor.
WebBrain'in önümüzdeki dönemdeki önceliklerinden biri tarayıcı ajanını günlük kullanımda daha güvenilir hale getirmek. Şirket özellikle küçük modellerin cihaz üzerinde çalışması, yapay zeka kullanım maliyetlerinin düşürülmesi ve kullanıcının hangi modeli kullanacağına kendisinin karar verebilmesi üzerine çalışmaya devam edecek.
Murshid tarafında ise yapay zeka ajanının tarayıcıya daha derin şekilde entegre edilmesi hedefleniyor. Akıllı sekme yönetimi ve tarama geçmişini kullanıcının cihazında tutarak çalışan bir hafıza sistemi planlanan özellikler arasında. Kurumsal kullanıcılar için geliştirilen WebBrain Cloud ise şu anda beta aşamasında.
WebBrain Cloud ile insanların ve yapay zeka ajanlarının birlikte kullanabileceği kalıcı tarayıcı oturumlarının oluşturulması, tarayıcı işlevlerine API üzerinden erişilmesi ve tekrar kullanılabilir iş akışlarının hazırlanması hedefleniyor. Tarayıcıların giderek yapay zeka ajanlarının doğrudan çalışma ortamına dönüştüğü günümüzde WebBrain; açık kaynak, yerel model desteği ve model bağımsızlığı üzerinden kendine farklı bir alan açmayı hedefliyor. Murshid ve WebBrain Cloud'un ekosisteme eklenmesiyle birlikte projenin yalnızca bir tarayıcı eklentisi olmaktan çıkarak daha kapsamlı bir yapay zeka tarayıcı altyapısına dönüşmeye çalıştığını söyleyebiliriz.

Sarah Wynn-Williams says tech insiders with concerns about AI are being silenced in system reminiscent of George Orwell’s 1984
The Meta whistleblower who made allegations about the social media company’s treatment of teenagers has urged Andy Burnham to go further in banning non-disclosure agreements, warning that tech insiders with concerns about AI development need to be protected.
Sarah Wynn-Williams, who served as the director of global public policy at Meta, then called Facebook , has been unable to talk about a series of allegations made in her memoir as a result of restrictions secured by the company.
The restrictions, which stem from a severance agreement Wynn-Williams signed after leaving Meta , mean she could face significant legal penalties for speaking about the company.
Giving the annual Orwell lecture in London, Wynn-Williams said she could not discuss her own case. However, she said NDAs had become a key weapon used by the powerful to keep “control over narrative”.
“The aim is not to win the argument,” she said. “The aim is to leave nothing to argue with. An absence. No record. No receipt. No contestable standard of truth. No common ground of fact against which anyone could measure those in power and expose their failures.”
She noted that NDAs appeared to have been used in the cases of both David Walliams , who faces allegations of sexual misconduct by several women, and Russell Brand, who was recently convicted of rape and sexual assault . Walliams denies the allegations against him.
“In both cases, there are reports of NDAs being deployed to silence women to ensure information that was clearly in the public interest was suppressed,” she said. “It may, allegedly, still be being suppressed.”
She welcomed the prime minister’s commitment to restrict the use of NDAs . Burnham said earlier this week that he was bringing forward changes to ensure victims of crimes or workplace harassment will have complete freedom over whom they can speak to, even if they have signed an NDA.
However, Wynn-Williams called on Burnham to go further by making the changes retrospective. She also called on the public to lobby for stronger action. “Change like this is hard,” she said. “And it is meaningful. It is an achievement that will impact people’s lives. But as the prime minister said, it is just the start.
“Tell your MP, your politically connected friend, your neighbour, it needs to go further. Make it retrospective, ban NDAs, allow people to speak. Even with this announcement, there will still be many with information that the public needs to know who are silenced.”
Wynn-Williams compared NDAs to the “memory hole” that George Orwell envisaged in his novel 1984 – a slot into which inconvenient documents are dispatched and destroyed.
She said action on NDAs was needed in relation to the rapid development of AI, to ensure insiders felt able to sound the alarm. “Parliaments, the press, the law – they’re all outside the building,” she said. “The people who know are on the inside. The researchers, the engineers, the ones who will say, ‘I was there. I know what I saw. I will warn’.
“They’re the ones we need to protect from the memory hole. But in order to get inside the building in the first place they needed to sign away their rights to speak.
“The technology industry has learned to buy silence by contract, the courts enforce the contract, and we are relying on those silenced by contract to warn us about its most dangerous product. That is the memory hole, installed in the place we can least afford it.”
Wynn-Williams made her allegations against Meta in a memoir, Careless People . However, under an interim arbitration ruling secured by Meta she is unable to speak about the book, which contains claims about Meta working with the Chinese government on censorship tools, and its negative impacts on teenagers.
She sat in silence on stage at the Hay literary festival in Wales earlier this year after taking legal advice, and is suing Meta over the restrictions it secured over her.
Meta strongly disputes Wynn-Williams’s book, saying it contains several false claims, and describes her legal case as a ploy to shift more copies.
“An NDA agreement is signed at the moment of maximum vulnerability, while the mortgage looms and the cardboard box of family photos sits in the front seat of the car,” Wynn-Williams said.
“It is signed by all types – from the C suite to the gig worker, the intern, the content moderator, the production assistant, the junior publicist, the stylist. There really is no better way to knock the whistle from someone’s lips.”

A Levski Sofia supporter has been filmed appearing to perform a Nazi salute in the stands during Marseille’s Europa League tie against the Bulgarian side, in footage that has circulated widely online. The clip emerged amid chaotic scenes at the Stade Vélodrome , where flares and other projectiles were thrown and rival supporters clashed before and during Thursday’s match.
Around 500 Levski fans were housed in the away section. About ten minutes before kick-off , several Marseille supporters ran from a home stand and breached the away enclosure, apparently targeting the Bulgarian fans. Projectiles and flares were thrown between the two groups, and further disturbances broke out during the half-time break.
Five Levski Sofia supporters were taken to hospital with injuries including eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder, according to the Marseille police prefecture . Around a dozen Bulgarian fans were reportedly injured in total. Despite the disturbances, the match kicked off as scheduled, with Marseille securing a 1-0 victory over the Bulgarian side.
The violence drew condemnation from French President Emmanuel Macron and his Bulgarian counterpart, Iliana Iotova . Levski Sofia coach Julio Velázquez also condemned the incidents, describing the scenes as “unacceptable for football” . The disturbances overshadowed the European fixture and renewed concerns over spectator safety at international club matches.

Fighting broke out ahead of Thursday's Europa League match between Levski Sofia and Olympique Marseille, with five Bulgarian fans ending up in hospital. Local media reported a number of Levski fans performing Nazi salutes in the lead-up to the skirmish.
Five Levski Sofia supporters were taken to hospital after violence ahead of the Europa League game at Marseille on Thursday, with the French and Bulgarian presidents blaming the home fans.
The lead-up to the match at the Stade Vélodrome was marred by confrontations in the stands between the two sets of fans, including the throwing of projectiles and flares.
Footage widely shared on social media showed a Levski supporter performing a Nazi salute in the direction of the Marseille fans before the violence broke out. Local media reports alleged the gesture was repeated by multiple Bulgarian fans in the lead-up to the skirmish.
Watch more Lyon held and Marseille pushed in mixed Europa League night for French clubs
The Marseille prosecutor's office said on Friday that it was investigating accusations that Marseille football fans committed "aggravated intentional violence" against visiting Bulgarian supporters.
Magistrates were also looking into allegations of "incitement to hatred after Nazi salutes and provocations from the Bulgarian fans" before the clashes broke out, it told AFP.
French President Emmanuel Macron condemned "in the strongest possible terms ... acts of violence targeting Bulgarian fans", the Élysée Palace said.
Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova called it "unacceptable" and "shocking".
"The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world," she said in a statement on Facebook.
"Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety."
Macron spoke to his Bulgarian counterpart on the sidelines of a European summit in Brussels , assuring her that "these acts would not go unpunished", the Élysée said.
Several hundred Marseille fans ran from the stand where they were situated about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Levski supporters.
They breached the stand designated for away fans, where around 500 visiting fans were gathered.
Fighting broke out, with several Marseille fans wearing face coverings, an AFP journalist at the scene said.
"Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder," a source with the Marseille police prefecture told AFP.
The police source said all the people injured were Bulgarian and there was "no information at this stage regarding any arrests".
Manuel Bompard, an MP for the left-wing France Unbowed (LFI) party for Marseille's Bouches-du-Rhône department, commented on a video shared online showing a Levski fan performing a Nazi salute.
"The far right has no place in our stadiums!" he wrote on X .
Iotova called on French authorities to "clarify the circumstances surrounding the attacks and look for responsibility from those who committed them".
She urged European football's governing body UEFA to "check how the safety of the Bulgarian fans at the stadium was ensured".
"We are ready to provide the necessary assistance to our compatriots. This behaviour is unacceptable!" she said.
Security personnel eventually managed to restore calm as the game kicked off on time.
There was another flare-up between opposing fans during half-time, before the match ended 1-0 to the hosts.
"It's a very regrettable episode – these are incidents which are unacceptable for football," said Levski coach Julio Velazquez.
"I support the fans who were caught up in this incident. I hope nothing serious has happened. I'm very saddened by this situation."
Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was "working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents".
"We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable," said Marseille coach Bruno Génésio.

Claims of Nazi salutes at UEFA Europa League game in Marseille headline night of further violence in European football.
Violent clashes at two European football matches have stoked concerns about fan violence and prompted the leaders of France and Bulgaria to condemn behaviour that had “no place in civilized Europe”.
Images showed masked ⁠and bloodied fans wielding improvised weapons and metal pipes during a brawl at a UEFA Europa League match on Wednesday evening between Marseille and Levski Sofia, which the Bulgarian club said began when their fans were attacked by supporters of the French side.
A photographer working for the Reuters news agency ⁠said the clashes at the Stade Velodrome in Marseille had started after a supporter from the visitors’ stand made a Nazi salute.
Clashes also broke out at a Europa League match in the Georgian city of Batumi between Turkiye’s Besiktas and Israel’s Hapoel Be’er Sheva, forcing the referee to suspend the match for 30 minutes.
European football’s governing body UEFA told Reuters its disciplinary body “would assess the match reports before considering any potential ‌next steps”.
Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said he and French President Emmanuel Macron spoke by phone and condemned the violence at the Marseille-Levski Sofia match, in which Marseille police said 11 Bulgarian fans were hurt, five of whom were taken to hospital.
“We share the position that aggression and violence have no place in civilized Europe,” Radev said on Facebook.
“I thank President Macron for his personal commitment to this case, for the medical care provided to the injured by the French authorities, for the measures taken to ensure the safety of Bulgarian citizens, and for the perpetrators to be held accountable.”
Macron said he had condemned “with the utmost ⁠force” acts of violence targeting Bulgarian fans, which he said had “no place in sport or in ⁠public space”, and told Radev they would not go unpunished.
A protest was planned in front of the French embassy in Sofia ⁠later on Friday.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said: “Violence, racial hatred and provocation have no place in our stadiums.”
Manuel Bompard, a French lawmaker for the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party in the Marseille department, commented on a video on social media appearing to show a Levski fan performing a Nazi salute.
“Congrats to the Marseille fans who responded with an antifascist chant,” Bompard wrote on X. “The far-right has no place in our stadiums!”
Levski Sofia, which lost the match 1-0, said masked fans had attacked its supporters with batons and flares. Some had let off flares and tried to get through ⁠the barrier as security staff tried to hold them back.
Images showed fans attacking each other through a netted fence separating sections of the stadium.
Before Thursday’s match, French authorities had introduced a sevenfold reduction of ticket sales to Levski supporters and imposed additional restrictions on their movement to and ⁠around the stadium, aiming to curb risks of violence.
The Bulgarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs said it would request a ⁠thorough investigation. Marseille said it would conduct its own analysis and was working closely ⁠with law enforcement.
The match between Besiktas and Hapoel Be’er Sheva had been moved from Istanbul for what UEFA said were safety and security reasons.
Clashes in the stands led referee Morten Krogh to suspend the match in the 26th minute, and it resumed after a 30-minute delay. Georgian police entered the stands, and television footage showed one ‌fan being carried out on a stretcher.
Turkish outlet NTV reported that police used pepper spray. Besiktas condemned what it called “disproportionate force” by security staff and said a number of fans had been denied entry. Besiktas went on to win 2-1.
Turkish Football Federation chair Ibrahim Haciosmanoglu defended the ‌decision ‌to keep Israeli clubs out of Turkiye following Israel’s invasion of Gaza in 2023 after the deadly Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel.
texts.https://webrazzi.com/2026/11/27/yapay-ze:
Bu hafta yapay zeka dünyasında gelişmiş modellerin kontrolü, bilimsel araştırmalarda yapay zeka kullanımı ve şirketlerin yeni ürünleri dikkat çekti. Anthropic ve OpenAI'ın matematik alanındaki çalışmaları gündeme gelirken Google DeepMind, Gemini 4 ajanlarıyla kuantum algoritmalarını geliştirdiğini duyurdu.
OpenAI, Anthropic, Google ve Meta'nın yeni araçları da haftanın önemli başlıkları arasında yer aldı. SAP'nin yapay zeka odaklı yeniden yapılanma planı, Nvidia'nın Güneydoğu Asya'ya yönelik sevkiyatları durdurması ve yapay zeka şirketlerinin yatırım faaliyetleri gündemi hareketlendirdi.
xAI'ın kurucu ekibinde yer alan Guodong Zhang, Zihang Dai ve Manuel Kroiss, gelecekteki olayları tahmin edebilen yapay zeka sistemleri geliştirmek amacıyla Epochal'ı kurdu . Şirketin ilk ürünü Time Portal, yapay zeka ajanlarının interneti geçmişteki belirli bir tarihte olduğu haliyle incelemesini sağlıyor. 30 yılı aşkın internet geçmişinden bir trilyondan fazla web sayfasını kapsayan sistem, ajanların geçmişteki bilgilerle geleceğe yönelik tahminler yapabilmesini hedefliyor.
Axios'ın 24 Kasım tarihli haberine göre Anthropic ve OpenAI'daki bazı çalışanlar, henüz kamuya sunulmayan yapay zeka modellerinin güvenli bir şekilde kullanıma açılıp açılamayacağını tartışıyor. İki düzineden fazla kaynağa dayandırılan haberde, şirket içindeki modellerin matematik, bilim, siber güvenlik ve yapay zeka araştırmalarında önemli ilerlemeler kaydettiği belirtiliyor. Bazı araştırmacılar, modellerin davranışlarını izlemenin ve kontrol etmenin giderek zorlaştığını savunuyor. OpenAI, yeni güvenlik gerekliliklerinin model yayımlama süreçlerini yavaşlatabileceğini belirtirken Anthropic, bir modelin şirket içinde tutulmasının tek başına güvenli olduğu anlamına gelmediğine dikkat çekiyor.
OpenAI'ın baş bilim insanı Jakub Pachocki, gelişmiş yapay zeka modellerinin yetenekleri artarken şirketlerin bazı sınırlar konusunda anlaşması gerektiğini savundu . Pachocki, yapay zeka sistemlerinin davranışlarını izleme ve değerlendirme araçları yeterince gelişene kadar bazı araştırma ve geliştirme faaliyetlerinin sınırlandırılmasını öneriyor. Bu yaklaşım, yapay zeka şirketlerinin güvenlik konusunda ortak standartlar belirlemesini hedefliyor.
Meta'nın yapay zekadan sorumlu üst düzey yöneticisi Alexandr Wang, yayımladığı yazıda süper zekanın gelişinin yaklaştığını savundu. Wang, yapay zeka modellerinin bilimsel araştırmalardaki ilerlemelerine işaret ederek sistemlerin yakın gelecekte kendi araştırma ve geliştirme süreçlerini yönetebilecek seviyeye ulaşabileceğini öne sürdü. Ancak insanlığın karar alma yetkisini yapay zekaya devretmemesi gerektiğini de vurguladı.
Anthropic CEO'su Dario Amodei, bazı şirket çalışanlarının gelecekte karar alma yetkisinin süper zeki yapay zekaya bırakılmasını desteklediğini ileri süren Axios haberine tepki gösterdi. Amodei, insanların yönetim ve karar alma yetkilerini yapay zekaya devretmesinin yanlış olduğunu belirtti. Bununla birlikte yapay zekanın yazılım geliştirme, ilaç araştırmaları ve ulaşım gibi belirli alanlarda daha bağımsız görevler üstlenmesini desteklediğini ifade etti.
Anthropic, şirket içinde geliştirilen bir Claude modelinin 1979'dan bu yana çözülemeyen Valiant varsayımına ilişkin bir matematiksel ispat ürettiğini duyurdu . VP ve VNP olarak bilinen matematiksel karmaşıklık sınıfları arasındaki ilişkiye odaklanan çalışma, bilgisayarların hangi problemleri verimli biçimde çözebileceğiyle ilgili temel sorulara yanıt arıyor. Claude'un hazırladığı çalışma ve Lean ile oluşturulan biçimsel ispat kamuya açılmış olsa da sonuç henüz bağımsız matematikçiler tarafından kapsamlı biçimde doğrulanmadı. Ayrıca bu çalışma, ünlü P ve NP probleminin çözüldüğü anlamına gelmiyor.
OpenAI, matematik araştırmalarında kullanılan yapay zeka sistemlerinin hazırladığı dokuz yeni makaleyi GitHub'da paylaştı . 24 Kasım'da yayımlanan çalışmalar, matris çarpımının hesaplama karmaşıklığı, matematiksel yapılar ve doğrusal programlama gibi konulara odaklanıyor. Şirket, bazı sonuçlar için Lean ile hazırlanmış biçimsel ispatlar da sundu. Ancak araştırmaların bağımsız akademik değerlendirme süreçleri henüz tamamlanmadı.
16 yaşındaki araştırmacı Cinna Davis, GPT-6.2 Astra'dan yararlanarak matematik alanındaki 100'den fazla açık problem için çözüm ve ispat çalışmaları hazırladığını duyurdu . Davis, yapay zeka ile oluşturulan sonuçları, karşı örnekleri ve doğrulama kodlarını GitHub üzerinden paylaştı. Bununla birlikte çalışmaların doğrulama seviyeleri farklılık gösteriyor ve tamamı bağımsız akademik incelemeden geçmiş değil.
OpenAI, GPT-6 ailesinin yalnızca akıl yürütme ve kodlama yeteneklerini kullanarak yeni protein yapıları ve amino asit dizilimleri tasarlayabildiğini gösteren araştırmasını yayımladı. Şirketin açıklamasına göre deneysel bir model, çeşitli protein tasarım görevlerinde bu alana özel geliştirilen modellerle benzer veya daha yüksek performans gösterdi. GPT-6.2 tarafından tasarlanan bazı proteinlerin hedef moleküllere bağlanabildiği laboratuvar testlerinde de gözlemlendi. OpenAI, araştırmanın ilaç keşfi ve biyoteknoloji alanlarında yeni kullanım olanakları yaratabileceğini belirtiyor.
Google DeepMind, Gemini 4 tabanlı yapay zeka ajanlarının birlikte çalışarak kuantum bilgisayarların kullandığı algoritmaları daha verimli hale getirdiğini duyurdu . Araştırmada ajanlar, dört saatte bir bir araya gelerek geliştirdikleri çözümleri karşılaştırdı ve yeni yöntemler üzerinde çalıştı. Google'ın paylaştığı sonuçlara göre füzyon enerjisi simülasyonlarına yönelik bir algoritmanın hesaplama maliyeti 11,8 kat azaltıldı.
OpenAI, ABD'deki küçük işletmelerin yapay zeka teknolojilerinden yararlanmasını kolaylaştırmak amacıyla OpenWorks programını tanıttı. 20 şehirde pilot olarak yürütülen program kapsamında teknik bilgiye sahip kişiler, küçük işletme sahiplerine yapay zeka araçlarını iş süreçlerine entegre etme konusunda destek veriyor. OpenAI, programa katılan yerel iş ortaklarına aylık 8 bin dolara kadar ödeme yapabiliyor.
OpenAI ve Cisco, Linux sistemlerindeki güvenlik açıklarına karşı koruma sağlamak amacıyla Shirudo adlı açık kaynaklı projeyi duyurdu . Shirudo, sistemler çalışmaya devam ederken bilinen güvenlik açıklarının kötüye kullanılmasını önlemeyi hedefliyor. Böylece güvenlik güncellemeleri hazırlanırken sunucuların yeniden başlatılmasına gerek kalmadan geçici koruma sağlanabiliyor.
Anthropic, kurumsal müşterilerine yönelik geliştirdiği Enterprise Frontier Safeguards çözümünü genel beta kullanımına açtı . Yeni sistem, şirketlerin hassas verilerini kendi bulut ortamlarında tutarken Claude'un gelişmiş güvenlik denetimlerinden yararlanmasını sağlıyor.
Google, Chrome'da çalışan yapay zeka ajanlarının güvenliğini değerlendirmek amacıyla Mirror Dimension adlı simüle edilmiş internet ortamını geliştirdi . Sistem, gerçek internet sitelerini taklit eden binlerce sayfa üzerinde ajanların davranışlarını test ediyor. Böylece yapay zeka ajanlarının güvenlik açıkları ve kötü niyetli yönlendirmeler karşısındaki tepkileri, gerçek kullanıcıları etkilemeden değerlendirilebiliyor.
OpenClaw, yapay zeka ajanlarının günlük hayattaki görevleri ne kadar başarılı tamamladığını ölçen ShellBench testini duyurdu . Araştırmada 12 yapay zeka modeli, 100 farklı görev üzerinde toplam 53 bin 100 kez test edildi. GPT-6 Astra yüzde 62,5 başarı oranıyla ilk sırada yer aldı. Sonuçlar, en başarılı modellerin bile görevlerin yaklaşık yüzde 40'ını eksiksiz tamamlayamadığını gösterdi.
New York Valisi Kathy Hochul, çocuklarla konuşabilen yapay zeka sohbet botlarının bulunduğu oyuncakların üretilmesini, dağıtılmasını ve satılmasını beş yıl boyunca yasaklayan yasayı imzaladı . Kararın arkasında çocukların güvenliği, kişisel verilerin korunması ve yapay zeka sistemlerinin uygunsuz içerikler üretebilmesiyle ilgili endişeler bulunuyor. Heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding creating hazardous conditions for millions travelling for holiday
King tides and huge waves have been battering both coasts of the US during a turbulent Thanksgiving period, with severe weather threatening millions across the country. Along the California coast, king tides caused considerable damage. In Pacifica, south of San Francisco, large waves battered the coastline on Wednesday, destroying part of a pier and sending debris into the ocean.
The National Weather Service issued coastal flood warnings covering parts of the Pacific coastline and shorelines around San Francisco Bay and San Pablo Bay. Several beachfront properties in Pacifica have already experienced flooding, while authorities in Marin County temporarily issued an evacuation warning for residents of beachfront homes at Stinson Beach.
The high tides also affected southern California. San Diego recorded a tide of 8ft 11in (2.7 metres) on Wednesday morning, while Los Angeles experienced tides reaching approximately 8.19ft, potentially surpassing a record set at the end of October.
King tides are unusually high natural tides that occur when the gravitational forces of the sun and moon combine around their alignment with Earth. Their impact is being heightened by unusually warm Pacific waters associated with the 2026 super El Niño.
A Nor’easter has also been bringing severe weather across the eastern US. The system produced heavy rain, damaging winds and coastal flooding, creating hazardous conditions for millions of Americans travelling to celebrate the holiday.
The severity of the forecast forced an unprecedented decision in New York: Macy’s postponed its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day parade, originally scheduled for Thursday, until Saturday. It was the first time in the event’s history that the parade had been postponed because of weather. The decision was taken to safeguard performers and spectators, particularly given the dangers that powerful gusts pose to the parade’s enormous character balloons.
Meanwhile, significant fresh snowfall during the past week has transformed conditions across several major ski regions in the Alps, providing an excellent early season foundation for the new season. French resorts have been among the biggest beneficiaries. Reported accumulated snow depths on Thursday included approximately 120cm in the Tignes-Val d’Isère area, while substantial snowfall was recorded around Les Deux Alpes, Alpe d’Huez and the Les Trois Vallées. Further snowfall is forecast across parts of France, Switzerland, Italy and Austria, with several resorts expecting additional accumulations over the coming days.

Violent clashes marred a number of European football matches on Thursday night, with French President Emmanuel Macron condemning trouble at Marseille's home game against Levski Sofia.
There were also incidents at games between Turkish side Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Be'er-Sheva in Georgia and Sunderland's 1-1 home draw with Poland's Jagiellonia Bialystok.
Uefa says it has appointed ethics and disciplinary inspectors "to conduct investigations into the incidents and examine all available evidence" from the Marseille-Levski Sofia and Besiktas-Hapoel Be'er-Sheva games.
European football's governing body said it "strongly condemns the serious incidents of violence and disorder" at those ties.
It added: "Violence, aggression, hatred and any form of provocative, discriminatory or extremist behaviour have no place in football.
"Uefa competitions are founded on the principles of respect, fair play, integrity and safety."
In Marseille, the build-up to the Europa League match at the Stade Velodrome was affected by incidents in the stands, including the throwing of projectiles and flares between the two sets of supporters.
With 10 minutes to go until kick-off, several Marseille fans ran from a home stand, appearing to pursue a group of Levski Sofia supporters.
They breached the stand designated for away fans, which housed around 500 supporters of the Bulgarian domestic champions.
"Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder," said the Marseille police prefecture. "Six others were treated on site for various wounds."
Macron spoke to Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev about the incidents, with the French president condemning "with the utmost force these acts of violence, which have no place in sport or in public space", and reassured him that "these acts would not go unpunished".
According to news agency Reuters, Radev thanked Macron for his personal involvement following the "attack on Bulgarian citizens" and for the medical assistance provided to the victims.
Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova said she found video footage of the incidents "shocking" in a statement posted on social media.
"The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world," she added.
"Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety."
Police response to Besiktas fans' pro-Palestine banner 'unacceptable'
Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was "working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents".
The police source said all the people injured were Bulgarian and there was "no information at this stage regarding any arrests".
Security personnel managed to restore calm, allowing the game to kick-off on time, although there were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break in a match Marseille won 1-0.
"It's a very regrettable episode. These are incidents which are unacceptable for football," said Levski Sofia coach Julio Velazquez
Marseille boss Bruno Genesio added: "We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable."
Besiktas fans clash with Georgian police at their game against Israeli side Hapoel Be'er-Sheva
Meanwhile, the Turkish Football Federation has strongly condemned the "unacceptable" actions of Georgian police towards Besiktas fans who unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner during their Europa League match against Israeli side Hapoel Be'er-Sheva.
Besiktas say they have lodged a complaint with European football's governing body Uefa over "disproportionate" use of force by Georgian police.
The match had been moved from Istanbul to Batumi, Georgia for safety and security reasons but had to be suspended in the 25th minute after clashes involving Besiktas supporters and local police.
Both the officiating team and the Besiktas players left the field, but play was able to resume 30 minutes later.
"We strongly condemn the unacceptable attitudes, behaviour and actions directed at Besiktas supporters inside and outside the stadium before and during the Uefa Europa League match," said a statement from the Turkish federation.
Turkish outlet NTV reported that Georgian police had gone into the stands and used pepper spray on the Besiktas fans.
The report added that there were anti-Israeli chants from the Turkish fans and that Besiktas players and director of football Onder Ozen spoke to supporters to try to calm matters before play restarted.
Hakan Fidan, Turkey's minister of foreign affairs, spoke to his Georgian counterpart Maka Botchorishvili following the incident.
"All necessary steps are being taken to ensure the safety of our citizens and protect their rights," a Turkish foreign ministry source said.
At Sunderland, there were crowd disturbances after Jagiellonia Bialystok fans were found in areas of the Stadium of Light with home fans, despite Uefa having imposed an away supporter ban for the Europa League game.
Police and stewards attended some disruption early on during the match.
"In the build-up to the match, the club had put measures in place in line with this sanction and maintained regular communication with our supporters, Jagiellonia Bialystok and Uefa," said a Sunderland statement.
"Unfortunately, Jagiellonia Bialystok failed to engage and cooperate on this matter.
"We are disappointed that these measures and communications were disregarded by some visiting supporters and we will review the circumstances surrounding their entry into the stadium."

Watch: Roofs torn off and streets under water as severe weather hits the US
Hundreds of thousands of people are without power after severe weather hit both coasts of the United States during the Thanksgiving holiday.
Eastern areas were lashed on Thursday by a powerful storm which brought high winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding. Pennsylvania remained the state worst hit by power cuts early on Friday, according to monitoring site Poweroutage.us.
Conditions are now expected to improve, though forecasters caution that it will take some time. The West Coast has also been affected by its own storms.
Flight disruption also persists, with hundreds more delays and cancellations reported on Friday - which is expected to be another busy travel day.
More than 2,500 flights within, into or out of the US were delayed on Thursday, and more than 450 were cancelled, according to Flightaware.com.
One passenger told the BBC he had been stuck at New York's LaGuardia Airport for 13 hours while trying to fly to see friends in Chicago for Thanksgiving.
Beyond the travel disruption, impacts were widespread across the East Coast, and US President Donald Trump said he would consider releasing emergency funds.
Bridges closed in Maryland due to severe winds, while waves battered beaches in Delaware as water seeped onto the boardwalk.
On the wettest Thanksgiving on record in Washington DC, tidal waters surged and soaked runways at Reagan Washington National Airport.
Parts of some states are under states of emergency, including New York.
Nearly 2in (5cm) of rain fail on New York City's iconic Central Park, making it the wettest Thanksgiving on record at that site as well, according to preliminary data , external from the NWS.
Organisers of the city's annual Macy's Thanksgiving parade have also pushed back the event to Saturday - marking the event's first postponement 100-year history.
In neighbouring New Jersey, there were multiple reports of closed roads and bridges, and images of floodwater blanketing city streets.
"This is wild," an Ocean City, New Jersey-based blogger said in a video , external posted on social media, as he waded through water splashing above his waist.
The number of homes reporting power cuts peaked at close to a million on Thursday evening - with Pennsylvania, Virginia, Maryland and New Jersey badly affected.
Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro said utility providers were working tirelessly to restore power. In Maryland, almost two million customers were asked by authorities to limit their water consumption to essential use only due to "intermittent power disruptions".
The storm is expected to ease on Friday and move into the Canadian provinces of Nova Scotia and Newfoundland on Saturday, leaving a much drier weekend for the north-eastern United States, according to the Met Office.
However, another deep area of low pressure will likely arrive on Monday - bringing another spell of heavy rain and strong winds, and some further travel disruption.
The particularly high tide in California caused huge waves to crash over the wall in Pacifica, where a portion of the municipal pier collapsed
On the West Coast, the concern was for exceptionally high tides and the associated risk of flooding.
Both San Diego and Los Angeles reported a high tide of over 8ft (2.4m) earlier this week, and beach-goers were advised to avoid coastal areas.
Train services along the Amtrak Pacific Surfliner, which runs along the California coastline, cancelled several trains due to "washout conditions from high tides", the company shared on social media.
Dramatic footage from Oregon showed a man and a dog being swept into the sea by a fierce, so-called king tide - but both escaped unharmed, police said.
Watch: Man and dog narrowly escape powerful king tide in Oregon
In Miami, some travel delays persisted into Thursday after a FedEx plane overshot the runway the night before, which prompted the closure of all but one runway at the airport for a brief period.
A statement FedEx provided to US media confirmed that one of its flights had "experienced an issue upon landing". No injuries were reported, and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is investigating what happened.
An airport employee who spoke anonymously to CBS News, the BBC's US partner, raised the possibility that rainy conditions had been a factor.
The American Automobile Association (AAA) predicted that 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles (80km) from home for the Thanksgiving holiday over a seven-day period.

Emmanuel Macron said it would be a "strategic mistake" to reduce EU spending
European Union (EU) leaders have deferred negotiations on its long-term budget after tensions surfaced over the bloc's spending priorities and aid for Ukraine.
Tense talks on the 2028-34 budget ended after 12 hours on Thursday at a summit in Brussels, with some members walking out of negotiations that will resume in December.
Divisions were largely split along the lines of countries, including France and Italy, wanting to approve a higher-spending proposal against those advocating for financial restraint, with Germany chief among them.
Many members want the budget locked in ahead of several high-stakes elections held across Europe in 2027, including in France.
Countries remain divided over a proposal to provide Ukraine with an additional loan of €45bn (£37.6bn), split between non-military and military funding.
Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Hungary have objected to the loan, but German Chancellor Frederich Merz said uniform EU agreement was a condition for approving the broader budget.
"I stand by my view that aid for Ukraine must be supported by the European Union as a whole," Merz told reporters.
"The European Union comprises of 27 member states, not 23 or 24."
Bulgaria, which previously opposed the plan, said it would agree to fund part of the loan that commits non-military financial support to Kyiv, marking a small sign of progress emerging from the special summit of the European Council.
EU members have been wrangling over the long-term budget after the European Commission submitted a €2tn proposal earlier this year, with some countries objecting to high levels of spending.
Those advocating higher spending want the funds to future-proof industries such as farming and invest in regional development. Fiscally cautious countries want to avoid amassing ballooning debt.
Thursday's talks were set up by the European Council to unblock the impasse, with a proposal to reduce spending by approximately €220bn to €230bn.
Under the current proposal, the budget totals €1.582tn, which includes €140bn to repay pandemic-era borrowing.
Four countries wanting to rein in the budget, including Denmark and Austria, walked out of negotiations after several hours of meetings.
Merz said there was "new movement" towards reducing the size of the EU budget, though he added "we are not there yet" when he confirmed that a new round of negotiations would not take place in Brussels on Friday.
European budgets requires approval from all 27 countries, with each country effectively holding veto power.
French President Emmanuel Macron said it would be a "strategic mistake" to lower long-term spending.
France's forthcoming presidential election came into focus during the EU budget talks, with frontrunner Marine Le Pen calling the talks an "underhanded political manoeuvring to thwart the democratic will of the French people".
Last month, Le Pen announced she would significantly reduce French aid to Ukraine and EU contributions if she were to win the presidency.
Macron addressed Le Pen's remarks on the sidelines of the Brussels summit, saying: "It is an odd kind of arrogance to behave as if she is already in charge of France's destiny because, as things stand, she has not been elected."
Once the talks concluded, the European Council announced a two-day summit on 17 and 18 December would revive budget negotiations.
Spanish economist Pablo Hernández de Cos was also named as the next President of the European Central Bank, replacing Christine Lagarde from February 2027.
texts.https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/27/eu-b:
Europe wants to become more independent, competitive and secure. Yet it is precisely the tasks that are crucial to this that face the deepest cuts in the draft for the next EU budget. Behind this lies a structural problem in European politics.
The special Brussels summit on the European budget for the years 2028 to 2034 ended without agreement. On 17 December, the heads of state and government will meet again. Until then, the main question will be how much Europe is prepared to spend.
The European Commission has proposed a financial framework of just under €2 trillion. Council President António Costa has reduced this to around €1.78 trillion. Germany and other net contributors still consider that too high.
More revealing than the overall figure, however, is where Costa makes the cuts. Compared with the Commission’s draft, he removes around €95.5 billion from competitiveness, prosperity and security, and around €54 billion from agriculture, cohesion and related tasks. That amounts to reductions of 16 and 5% respectively. In defence industry, security and space, the cuts are almost 30%.
Costa’s draft does foresee substantial increases for defence and competitiveness compared with the current budget. Even so, the new strategic priorities are being cut disproportionately.
Germany and other net contributors want to limit their payments and focus the budget more strongly on competitiveness and security. Poland and other cohesion countries defend the funding for their regions. France wants an ambitious European budget while also protecting its agriculture. Italy takes a sceptical view of additional European levies.
Each of these positions is understandable from a national perspective. The problem arises from how they interact.
The European financial framework requires unanimity in the Council and the consent of the European Parliament. Every government can make its approval conditional on its own interests being safeguarded. This favours spending whose benefits can be clearly attributed to individual member states.
A French president can explain to farmers which subsidies he has secured in Brussels. A Polish prime minister can point to new roads and modernised regions. But which head of government can claim the benefit of a joint European air defence system purely for his or her own country?
Joint European tasks do have political advocates. But their benefits are less easily mapped onto the national balance sheet that underpins almost every budget negotiation in the end: how much did we pay in, and how much do we get back?
About 60% of the current European financial framework is devoted to agriculture and cohesion. Both areas serve core purposes of European integration: food security, economic development and the reduction of regional disparities.
However, Europe now has additional tasks to tackle that did not carry anything like the same weight when this budget structure was created.
Russia is threatening Europe’s security order. China has built up significant technological and industrial capacity in strategic sectors. The United States is pursuing its own economic and security interests, which do not necessarily coincide with Europes.
The conditions under which the bloc has built its prosperity in recent decades are changing fundamentally.
That cannot be addressed simply through higher national defence spending. It is equally about joint defence research, industrial production capacity, secure supply chains, cross-border energy networks, military mobility and European expertise in key technologies.
In 2024 Mario Draghi set out what would be needed: catching up the innovation gap with the United States and China, combining decarbonisation with competitiveness, and strengthening Europe’s security by reducing strategic dependencies. He put the additional private and public investment required at €750 to 800 billion a year.
This sum cannot and should not be financed solely from the European budget. However, the budget can mobilise national and private investment and make joint projects possible where individual member states cannot achieve the necessary scale on their own.
I believe the European budget should be shaped much more by its tasks. The decisive factor should be what the member states can achieve better, more efficiently or more cheaply together than alone.
Agriculture and the less developed regions of Europe still need reliability. But their shares of the budget should, with appropriate transition periods, gradually yet clearly decline in order to create more scope for joint investment in the future.
Anyone who thinks Europe can simply carry on as before is living off a substance that is steadily shrinking. A Europe that wants to become more sovereign and more independent also has to get ahead of events.
That calls for honesty on the revenue side. Costa’s draft sets aside €158 billion solely for repaying the EU debt taken on during the pandemic. This money is not available for other tasks.
Costa therefore proposes additional European sources of revenue, including levies on digital services provided by large companies, on tobacco and on non-recycled electronic waste. Anyone who rejects additional own resources has to explain whether they prefer higher national contributions or corresponding cuts. And anyone who demands more European tasks has to say how they should be funded.
The contribution rebates also belong in this context. They are the expression of a budget logic that measures the success of European policy by national returns. As long as this calculation dominates, funding joint tasks will remain structurally more difficult.
Germany and France are pushing for an understanding before the end of the year. Given the French presidential election next spring, that is understandable.
One possible compromise would be an even smaller overall volume combined with concessions to the net contributors, agriculture and the cohesion countries. Particularly contentious sources of revenue could be postponed, and funding for further aid to Ukraine could be negotiated separately.
Such an agreement would carry weight. It would create planning certainty and show that 27 governments, despite differing interests, are capable of reaching a compromise.
The crucial question, however, would be the price at which it is achieved. If the main effect is to protect established spending while once again making the new strategic tasks bear most of the savings, the underlying problem would remain.
Europe would still have to tackle many of its new tasks largely through national budgets, loans and additional financing instruments. Especially for long term investment in security, infrastructure and technological competitiveness, a lack of joint planning can lead to higher costs and avoidable duplication.
We do not have to turn all our challenges into European ones. But we should organise and fund at European level those we can no longer adequately handle at national level.
Anyone who wants a more sovereign and more independent Europe must also be prepared to draw fiscal policy conclusions from that.
